courses.description: Introduces concepts, approaches, tools, methods for extracting useful knowledge and business value from data for business applications. Covers predictive models, descriptive models, model fitting, model overfitting, complexity, visualization, text mining, association mining, analytical thinking. Other topics may include social network mining, data science and business strategy. Students cannot receive credit for this course and CSE 145 .
courses.raw_requirements: Prerequisite(s): CSE 30 ; and MATH 22 or MATH 23A or AM 30 ; and STAT 5 , or STAT 7 and 7L, or STAT 17 and STAT 17L , or STAT 131 , or CSE 107 .

courses.title: Introduction to Data Mining for Business

courses.description: Introduction to optimization theory, numerical algorithms, and applications focused on operations research topics. The course content includes: linear programming, integer programming, non-linear programming, and an introduction to relevant simulations.
courses.raw_requirements: Prerequisite(s): AM 10 or MATH 21 , and AM 30 or MATH 22 or MATH 23A .
courses.subject: TIM
courses.title: Optimization for Management

courses.description: Uses weekly talks by leading industry practitioners and university researchers to provide in-depth exposure to the management of technology. Topics covered include product development, operations, strategy, finance, and marketing for technologies such as software and information systems. (Formerly CSE 170.)
courses.subject: TIM
courses.title: Management of Technology Seminar

courses.description: Addresses strategic, engineering, marketing, and financial processes and tools for the management, development, and commercialization of high-tech products. Declared TIM majors must concurrently enroll in TIM 172P to fulfill the capstone series. (Formerly CSE 171A.)
courses.raw_requirements: Prerequisite(s): MATH 19B or MATH 20B or MATH 11B or AM 11B or ECON 11B.
courses.subject: TIM
courses.title: Introduction to Management of Technology I

courses.description: Addresses the development and application of processes and tools for the management, design, optimization, and operation of supply chain networks for high-tech products. Declared TIM majors must concurrently enroll in TIM 172Q to fulfill the capstone series. (Formerly CSE 171B.)
courses.subject: TIM
courses.title: Introduction to Management of Technology II

courses.description: First of a two-course project sequence in which students apply the knowledge and skills gained in TIM 172A to complete the first part of a major quarter-long comprehensive team project in the management of technology. In this course, taken concurrently with TIM 172A , the team project focus is on the management, design, and commercialization of a new product within a high-tech company. TIM 172A and TIM 172P together form the first part of the required management of technology comprehensive requirement for the TIM B.S. major.
courses.raw_requirements: Prerequisite(s): concurrent enrollment in TIM 172A . Enrollment is restricted to Technology and Information (TIM) majors.
courses.subject: TIM
courses.title: Management of Technology Project I

courses.description: Second of a two-course project sequence in which students apply the knowledge and skills gained in TIM 172B to complete the second part of a major comprehensive team project in the management of technology. In this course, taken concurrently with TIM 172B, the team project focus is on the supply chain management for the new product developed in TIM 172P. TIM 172B and TIM 172Q together form the second part of the required management of technology comprehensive requirement for the TIM B.S. major.
courses.raw_requirements: Prerequisite(s): TIM 172A and TIM 172P. Concurrent enrollment in TIM 172B is required.
courses.subject: TIM
courses.title: Management of Technology Project II

courses.description: Addresses methods and tools for financing technology development and projects. Includes approaches for coordinating finance and accounting with strategy and operations of firms; discounted cash-flow analysis; activity-based costing; financial planning; and elements of financial account and investment science. (CSE 173.)
